## ROOT CAUSE PROVEN — it is the SCHEMA, not the plan. And it is a REGRESSION introduced 2026-08-05 00:48.

### The mechanism (one changeable artifact)

`_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES` in `src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py` carries an exact-id row

    "us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6": {
        "native_structured_output": True,
        "native_output_with_thinking": True,
    },

added by [rebar:18ae-27e9-b651-4b71] in commit `6c8daf7945` ("18ae: native output for measured
Bedrock cells", **2026-08-05 00:48**). That row is applied AFTER the `_REBAR_OVERRIDES` family rule
`(_is_claude -> native_structured_output: False)` and therefore **wins**, flipping this model from
rebar's deliberate `PromptedOutput` posture to `NativeOutput`.

`NativeOutput` sends the contract's JSON Schema to Bedrock for **constrained decoding**. The
plan-review Pass-2 prerequisite verifier binds `plan_review_verification` — the **largest contract in
the registry at 8,719 bytes** (`VerificationOutput{verifications: list[Verification{index, analysis,
severity_attributes: PlanSeverityAttrs(13 fields incl. a 4-way Literal), binary: Binary(8 fields)}]}`).
Bedrock cannot compile that grammar inside its own budget and returns HTTP 400
`ValidationException`.

So the chain is: **exact-id override -> NativeOutput -> 8.7 KB schema -> Bedrock grammar compilation
fails -> 400 -> every finding degrades to `no-verification` -> INDETERMINATE, unsigned, ticket
unclaimable.**

### The discriminating experiment (live, us-east-1, one session, one model)

Three calls that differ in exactly one variable:

| # | contract | mode | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| E3 | a 2-field `Tiny` model | **NativeOutput** | **OK in 2.0s** |
| E1 | `plan_review_verification` (8,719 B) | **NativeOutput** | **FAIL in 185.3s** — 400 "Grammar compilation timed out" |
| E2 | `plan_review_verification` (8,719 B) | **PromptedOutput** (rebar's normal Claude path) | **OK in 11.2s**, parsed to 1 verification |

E3 vs E1 isolates the schema: same model, same region, same credentials, same process — only the
contract changes. E1 vs E2 isolates the output mode and **proves the remedy direction works today**.

This rules out every rival explanation: provider flakiness, account/region load, credentials, plan
text, plan size, and finding count.

### Bedrock states the cause itself

The same step returns **two different** provider messages for the same schema:

* `The model returned the following errors: Grammar compilation timed out.` (~185s)
* `The model returned the following errors: Schema is too complex.` (~49-65s)
  — e.g. `/tmp/03ef-review4.out`, `/tmp/rp94a3c.log`

"Schema is too complex" is the provider naming the defect directly.

### Temporal proof it is a regression

* Override landed **00:48**. First live 400: **01:02** (`/tmp/4ca2_rev1_err.log`) — 14 minutes later.
* **Zero** occurrences in any captured log before 00:48.
* The failure duration is pinned at **180.6-185.9s** across 27 occurrences (mode ~185.6s). A constant
  wall-clock is a server-side compile budget, not load variance.

### CORRECTION to my earlier comment on this ticket

My previous comment reported "14 runs clean, 2 failing, correlates with finding count, candidate
threshold between 10 and 15 findings." **That is wrong and I withdraw it.** A wider sweep of the
captured logs finds **27 live 400s across at least 9 distinct review targets** — 4ca2 (x11), bf31
(x2), 03ef (x3), rp94a3 (x3), c827 (x2), aec1 (x2), and others — not two tickets.

Two errors produced the wrong conclusion:

1. I scanned a hand-picked set of 16 logs and generalised from it.
2. I inferred "14 runs succeeded" from the ABSENCE of a failure line. Success is logged at INFO and
   those captures are WARNING-only, so a successful call **cannot appear** in them. The absence was
   an artifact of log level, not evidence of success.

The finding-count correlation was a coincidence of which tickets happened to be reviewed. The real
discriminator is whether a run reaches the prerequisite-verify step at all.

### Blast radius — this is NOT confined to plan-review

Every registered contract's schema, measured locally:

    8719  plan_review_verification        <- the proven failure
    7995  code_review_verification        <- nearly identical size; code-review gate at risk
    5342  verification
    4022  completion_verdict
    2479  review_result
    ... 14 smaller contracts

Any structured step on this model binding a large contract is exposed. A size ladder is being
measured live to establish the actual boundary; results to follow.

### Two independent defects, not one

1. **The routing defect (primary).** rebar sends Bedrock a grammar it cannot compile. 18ae enabled the
   row on the strength of E1 measurements that used SMALL contracts — the measurement never covered
   the largest contract in the codebase, so the row overreaches its own cited evidence.
2. **The failure-handling defect (secondary, already AC1/AC3 here).** A schema-complexity 400 is a
   PERMANENT, deterministic property of the request — retrying is guaranteed to fail, and it did, 27
   times, at ~185s each (~83 minutes of wall clock burned). It is currently surfaced as a generic
   provider failure and degrades every finding to `no-verification` with no partial credit, even when
   `blocking: 0`.

### Incidental finding (separate ticket material)

The direct-Anthropic fallback is non-functional in this environment: `overlap-judge` and
`plan-review-prerequisite-verifier` both show `status_code: 401 ... 'API key is invalid.'` against
`anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6` (`/tmp/03ef-review6.out`). So when Bedrock rejects the schema, the
fallback chain cannot rescue the call either.

### Legitimacy: `defect` (regression)

Cited: behaviour that worked before `6c8daf7945` and broke after it; and 18ae's own scope statement
("Enable exactly the measured cells") — the measured evidence did not include an 8.7 KB contract, so
the row asserts a capability that was never measured for this payload class.
